§9.2.6 Horizontal Slicing

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-horizontal-slicing · tables continuation boundaries

✅ Normative

A table too wide for the page, printed as stacked column blocks, MUST be rendered as one table per printed block, each keeping its repeated row-label column. The blocks MUST NOT be re-widened into a single wide table.

A table too wide for the page is printed as column blocks stacked vertically, with the row-label column repeated in each block.

| State | Jan | Feb | Mar |
| AL    | 1.1 | 1.2 | 1.2 |

| State | Apr | May | Jun |   ← same rows, next columns
| AL    | 1.3 | 1.3 | 1.4 |

Requirements

  • Each printed block MUST be rendered as its own table, top to bottom.
  • The repeated row-label column MUST be kept in every block. It is printed in each one, and it is what makes the blocks joinable later.
  • The blocks MUST NOT be re-widened into a single State | Jan…Jun table, even though the repeated key makes the join look obvious.

How to recognise it

The blocks share their rows and differ in their columns — the same keys reappear down each block, with new column headers over them. That is the opposite of Column Continuation§9.2.2, where the blocks share their columns and the key runs onward from one block to the next.

If the row keys do not line up across the blocks, it is not a slice of one wide table at all: the blocks are separate tables, with no join to look for.

The asymmetry worth noticing

In Column Continuation§9.2.2, widening is the one shape that is always wrong: it pairs unrelated records with each other. Here it is the appealing option, because the repeated key column gives a reliable join and no record gets paired with a stranger. The rendering nevertheless stays one table per printed block: the page printed blocks, and the join is left to whoever consumes the output.

Related

  • Column Continuation§9.2.2 — the transpose: blocks side by side, key running onward
  • Cross-Page Tables§4.3 — blocks split by a page break instead of by width
  • Repeated Headers and Title Bands§9.2.7 — a header printed again below data rows opens a new table
